summary: Reviewed 2 source files (mcp-server/gui/server.ts, mcp-server/gui/api.ts) plus test additions (mcp-server/tests/gui/api.test.ts). OWASP Top 10 reviewed. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info. Security sign-off: PASS. The inline SAFE_SLUG_REGEX.test() pattern at the routing layer (AC3 concern) is confirmed acceptable: it uses the identical regex as assertSafeSlug(), is applied after decodeURIComponent() (correct order), and provides early rejection before any I/O. The unused repoName parameter introduces no security gap within WP-009 scope; routing-layer validation and project-existence check (resolveRepoName) are both enforced before handler invocation.

comments.note: A01/A03 (path traversal, defence-in-depth): In all new /:repo/:slug routes, decodeURIComponent() is called at route-dispatch time (outside the async closure) but SAFE_SLUG_REGEX.test() runs inside the returned async closure. This means a route closure is allocated even for invalid slugs — rejection still happens before any filesystem access, so there is no exploitable window. The ordering is safe but slightly inconsistent with the comment 'applied before any handler call'. No code change required; worth noting for future route authors.

A03 (future scope — WP-011): The repository_name value read from .meta.json by resolveRepoName() is passed as repoName to handler bodies starting in WP-011. At that point, repoName must be validated (e.g. via assertSafeSlug or equivalent) before it is used in any path.join() call in handler bodies. The routing-layer SAFE_SLUG_REGEX check validates the URL segment (repoUrlParam) but .meta.json → repository_name could theoretically differ. WP-011 implementer: call assertSafeSlug(repoName) in handlers before using repoName in filesystem paths.

A01/A03 (info, pre-existing, not introduced by WP-009): The filename parameter in dialogue/chunk routes (/:slug/dialogues/:filename, /:repo/:slug/dialogues/:filename, etc.) is decoded via decodeURIComponent at dispatch time but not validated against a safe pattern at the routing layer. Defence relies on handler-level containment. This is pre-existing behaviour; WP-009 did not introduce it. Recommend a future work item to add a filename allowlist regex at the routing layer (e.g. restrict to alphanumeric, hyphens, dots) to provide defence-in-depth.

AC3 confirmed acceptable: SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/) is an anchored allowlist that rejects all path traversal inputs (.., /, \, %, null bytes, uppercase, non-ASCII) after decodeURIComponent expansion. The inline check in server.ts is functionally identical to assertSafeSlug() (same imported constant, same failure mode — ApiError NOT_FOUND). Applying it at the routing layer rather than only in handler bodies is a net security improvement.

server.ts: The /:repo/:slug route closures each inline the same 3-line guard:
  if (!SAFE_SLUG_REGEX.test(repoUrlParam) || !SAFE_SLUG_REGEX.test(slug)) throw ...
  const repoName = await resolveRepoName(...);
This pattern is repeated 15+ times. A future helper `async function validateAndResolve(ledgerRoot, repo, slug)` would eliminate the duplication. Not blocking — intentional routing-layer design confirmed by Security Auditor — but worth extracting if a maintenance cycle passes.

server.ts: The keyword exclusion guards (rest[2] !== 'plan' && rest[2] !== 'synthesis' && ...) on routes with rest.length === 4 are redundant. These guards are necessary on the catch-all at rest.length === 3 (to avoid shadowing flat /:slug/keyword routes), but length-4 routes cannot collide with length-3 flat routes. The guards are harmless but add visual noise. The Developer's own comment 'does not conflict with /:slug/keyword (length 3)' confirms this. Safe to remove on next maintenance pass.
